findings.evidence: ## Reference routing: "Do NOT load feedback-sbi-model.md for a single straightforward opener..." repeats the Load column in the Section 2 table (lines 24-29). Section 4 and the Confidentiality test also restate general professional norms.
findings.fix: Delete the Reference routing section, or reduce it to one line that points to the Load column. Fold the Do-NOT-load guidance into the table cells so it is stated once.

findings.evidence: Section 4 (Receive) has three bullets and no worked reply, and references/ has no example for receiving feedback. The SBI, scope and conflict paths each have a worked example or script. The skill also mixes feedback, expectation reset and recap in one Process-style file with uneven depth.
findings.fix: Add a short receiving-feedback script, for example "Which project or date do you have in mind, and what was the effect?" Put it in a references/ file gated by a Load cell, or inline in about 5 lines.

findings.evidence: The Gotchas list has ten items. Several carry the reason inline, but the "Timing" item (line 74) gives no reason beyond the timing itself, and the "Feedback by chat or email" item (line 73) overlaps the "recap" item (line 72).
findings.fix: Merge the lines 72-73 items into one gotcha about retained written channels. Add the reason to the Timing item, for example that the person cannot absorb feedback or act on it before presenting or going on call.

findings.evidence: The description is dense and lists no scope-creep or thanks trigger. Its boundary names only difficult-workplace-conversations as a neighbour and gives no examples of what counts as a conversation with no feedback goal.
findings.fix: Prepare, deliver, receive and follow up on specific workplace feedback with Situation-Behavior-Impact (SBI), and reset stakeholder expectations with explicit scope/date trade-offs. Use when thanking or recognizing a teammate, raising an observable behavior (broken builds, missed commitments, interrupting), answering vague criticism such as "you're unreliable" even if the user never says feedback, prepping a 1:1 or upward feedback, giving feedback to two people in a conflict you lead, writing the follow-up recap, or pushing back on a deadline or scope creep. Not for legal or HR determinations, PIPs, ratings, policy drafting, or hard conversations with no feedback or expectation goal such as layoffs or salary talks (use difficult-workplace-conversations).

findings.evidence: The Load column gates the references (lines 24-29), but the receiving path says "nothing" (line 27). The "Do NOT load" sentence at line 85 duplicates the table instead of adding a rule.
findings.fix: Keep the gating in the Load column. Replace the Reference routing section with one sentence, or delete it, so each reference is gated in one place only.

findings.evidence: "Settle four things from the request, asking only for what is missing" leaves open how many clarifying questions to ask before drafting. Line 18 fixes the sub-case of impressions or hearsay, and the Section 6 follow-up check-ins give defaults. Nothing says whether to draft first and flag assumptions when the user is vague.
findings.fix: Add a default: if purpose and power are clear but evidence is thin, draft one opener with bracketed placeholders and ask for the one missing fact. Do not interrogate the user with four questions.

findings.evidence: The negatives are mostly easy and unrelated (keynote, survey, vendor contract, anniversary note). Only the Postgres/DynamoDB, PIP and academic-SBI queries are real near-misses. There is none for the declared neighbour difficult-workplace-conversations.
findings.fix: Replace two easy negatives with near-misses that name the neighbour boundary, for example "I have to tell someone their role is being eliminated tomorrow, how do I handle the conversation?" and "help me negotiate a raise with my manager".

findings.evidence: The Receive path says "agree to revisit when there is one" but gives no wording. The evals receiving-hostile-feedback case asks for a script and SKILL.md supplies none, so the agent has to invent the wording. Section 3 asks for a re-run of the dispute test with no output checklist.
findings.fix: Add a 3-line sample reply to a vague label in Section 4. Add a one-line pre-send checklist to Section 3: dispute test passed, no inferred motive, private delivery, confidentiality test passed.
